Description: New alert_subscriptions table in the existing TelegramSessionStore SQLite DB: chat_id, intent JSON (role_family/keywords/experience/city), active flag, created_at, last_sent_at, sent_job_ids JSON. Subscribe/unsubscribe/list/due APIs. One active subscription per chat (new subscribe overwrites — simplest honest model for 1.1). Must be migration-safe on an existing live DB, same pattern as guest_profiles.
Acceptance Criteria: Subscribe stores the exact intent the guest searched; resubscribe overwrites; unsubscribe deactivates without deleting history; due-query returns only active subs; store survives restart.
Definition of Done: APIs unit-tested including restart persistence and overwrite semantics; suite green.
Smart Checklist:
[ ] Schema + auto-migration on startup
[ ] subscribe_alert / unsubscribe_alert / list_alerts / due_alerts APIs
[ ] One-active-sub-per-chat overwrite rule
[ ] sent_job_ids dedupe field round-trips
[ ] Unit tests incl. restart + overwrite
[ ] No PII beyond what guest_profiles already stores

Description: After any successful results screen add '🔔 Alert me daily' action. Tap = confirmation message stating exactly what was saved (role · experience · city) + '🔕 Stop alerts' button. /stopalerts text command as backup path. Buttons follow the existing deterministic ButtonFlow patterns (BTN_PREFIX callbacks, stale-button self-heal).
Acceptance Criteria: Button appears only after real results (not on zero-result or waitlist screens); confirmation echoes the guest's own saved search in plain words; stop works from button AND /stopalerts; stale alert buttons never dead-end.
Definition of Done: Wired into ButtonFlow with tests for subscribe, confirm text, stop via button, stop via command, stale tap; suite green.
Smart Checklist:
[ ] 🔔 button on results screen
[ ] Confirmation with saved search echo
[ ] 🔕 Stop alerts button
[ ] /stopalerts command (works even mid-flow)
[ ] Stale-button fallback covered

Description: Beat/cron job that runs once daily AFTER the scrape+enrich window completes. For each due subscription: run the exact same deterministic _job_reply with the stored intent, filter out job ids already in sent_job_ids, send up to 10 new rows with canonical links, update last_sent_at + sent_job_ids. Zero new jobs = send nothing. Throttle sends (Telegram ~30 msg/s global) and space per-chat sends.
Acceptance Criteria: Alerts contain only never-sent verified jobs; zero-new = silence; dispatcher is idempotent (re-run after crash never double-sends); never runs during scrape or Ollama-hot periods; send bursts respect Telegram limits.
Definition of Done: Dispatcher unit-tested with fake API (dedupe, idempotency, zero-new silence, throttle); scheduled in beat after the scrape window; suite green.
Smart Checklist:
[ ] Beat schedule anchored after daily scrape completes
[ ] Reuse _job_reply — zero new fact paths
[ ] Per-sub dedupe via sent_job_ids
[ ] Idempotent re-run (crash-safe marker before send)
[ ] Zero-new = no message
[ ] Send throttling + per-chat spacing
[ ] Dispatch trace/log line per run

Description: When Telegram returns 403 (guest blocked the bot / deleted account), auto-pause that subscription instead of retrying forever. Dispatcher also re-checks the open-gate blocklist so an Ashok-blocked id never receives an alert.
Acceptance Criteria: A 403 pauses that sub after the failed send and is visible in owner stats; blocked ids are skipped before any send; other subs in the same run are unaffected by one failure.
Definition of Done: Tests for 403-pause, blocklist skip, and failure isolation; suite green.
Smart Checklist:
[ ] Catch 403 per send, pause sub
[ ] is_allowed re-check before each send
[ ] One failure never aborts the whole run
[ ] Paused subs visible to owner
[ ] Unit tests

Description: Risk logged before build: if the dispatcher crashes between send and sent_job_ids persist, a re-run could double-send the same jobs. Design decision: persist a per-sub 'dispatch attempt' marker BEFORE sending, reconcile on startup — verified by a kill-mid-run test.
Acceptance Criteria: Kill-the-dispatcher-mid-run test proves no guest ever receives the same job id twice for the same subscription.
Definition of Done: Regression test exists and is green before the epic closes.
Smart Checklist:
[ ] Attempt-marker design implemented
[ ] Kill-mid-run regression test
[ ] Startup reconcile path tested

Summary: [Preventive] Alert fires during scrape window / hot laptop
Description: Risk logged before build: a mis-anchored schedule could dispatch while the daily scrape or Ollama enrich is running, fighting the tower for resources (heat-pacing law). Dispatcher must gate on scrape-idle + heat state, deferring (not skipping) until safe.
Acceptance Criteria: Dispatcher defers when scrape is active or heat is critical and runs later the same day; deferral is logged and visible in /alerts.
Definition of Done: Gate + deferral covered by unit test; suite green.
Smart Checklist:
[ ] Scrape-idle gate
[ ] Heat-state gate (reuse existing heat pacing signals)
[ ] Defer-and-retry logic + test
